_comment: Tiered subagent model selection. Edit this file, not the hook code. See SPEC.md.
_disabledComment1: Tiers this account cannot use. `fable` requires specific access;
_disabledComment2: routing to a model you cannot run fails the spawn outright, so anything
_disabledComment3: listed here falls back to the next cheaper tier and the ledger records the
_disabledComment4: substitution as `+unavailable:fable->opus`. install.sh pre-populates this by
_disabledComment5: checking which models your transcripts show you have actually used.

catchAll._comment: Applied to general-purpose, claude, and any type not in agentTypes.

cheap._comment1: UNCHANGED 2026-09-16 after an attempt to extend it was reverted in full.
cheap._comment2: `verify`, `grade`, `confirm whether` and `you are a grader` were all tried
cheap._comment3: and removed: maxChars 300 is not the guard it looks like. 'Verify the crypto
cheap._comment4: protocol in protocol.md is sound.' is 58 characters and needs real judgement,
cheap._comment5: and 'You are a grader. Assess whether the protocol is sound.' scores
cheap._comment6: mechanical on the role phrase alone. Both would be redirected to scout,
cheap._comment7: whose prompt tells it to STOP when judgement is required — so the cost of a
cheap._comment8: false cheap match is a refused task, not a slightly worse answer.
cheap._comment9: Cheap matching is for bounded factual retrieval. A verb is not a rubric.

expensive._comment1: minChars promotes on LENGTH ALONE, so it must sit above the length of a
expensive._comment2: normal prompt or it fires on everything. Measured over 112 real spawns:
expensive._comment3: median 2692 chars, p75 3181, and only 2 fell under an earlier 1500 setting —
expensive._comment4: which made 'long' a constant, not a signal. 6000 sits above p75 and still
expensive._comment5: catches the genuinely sprawling briefs (longest observed: 8421).
expensive._comment6: Verbs removed as too common in routine prompts: audit, security, evaluate,
expensive._comment7: why. They fired on ordinary implement/review work and forced it to opus.

overrides._comment: Tags in the Agent description. Authoritative: they bypass both clamps.
overrides._comment2: Offload tag. Sends the spawn to an OpenAI model via the Codex CLI instead
overrides._comment3: of an Anthropic one. Authoritative like the other tags, and it wins over
overrides._comment4: them: [gpt] [hard] means a hard task run on Codex's top model.
overrides._comment5: Offload precedence is [gpt] > [agy] > [gemini] when a description has more than one tag.

redirect._comment1: Effort tiering. The Agent tool schema declares additionalProperties:false, so an
redirect._comment2: `effort` field cannot be injected per invocation — it would be rejected. Instead,
redirect._comment3: mechanical work is redirected to a custom agent definition that carries model AND
redirect._comment5: Only GENERIC agent types are redirected. Specialised built-ins such as Explore have
redirect._comment6: tuned system prompts worth keeping, so they only get their model set.
redirect._comment10: fable -> architect added 2026-09-16. Measured: 31 paired tag:hard spawns
redirect._comment11: burned $690.82 (47% of all spend) at 41k median output over 47 median turns.
redirect._comment12: looks_failed was 0%, but that only means no refusal phrase matched — it is
redirect._comment13: NOT evidence the extra turns were wasted. Treat medium as an experiment and
redirect._comment14: judge it on rework and escaped defects, not on the same weak proxy.
redirect._comment15: architect.md keeps model fable but declares effort medium, which is the only
redirect._comment16: way to lower effort on the Agent path. Forks are unaffected: they inherit the
redirect._comment17: parent model and never reach this gate.
redirect._comment7: sonnet -> worker is deliberately off by default: sonnet is the base case for a lot
redirect._comment8: of varied work, and worker's prompt assumes the approach is already decided. Set it
redirect._comment9: to "worker" once the ledger shows how those spawns actually behave.

codex._comment1: Offload to OpenAI models through the Codex CLI. Verified 2026-09-16:
codex._comment2: `codex` auth_mode is `chatgpt`, i.e. a flat-rate subscription rather than
codex._comment3: per-token API billing — so an offloaded spawn costs nothing against the
codex._comment4: Anthropic usage window beyond the haiku relay agent that drives it.
codex._comment5: Mechanism: the gate rewrites subagent_type to the `codex` agent, sets model
codex._comment6: haiku, and prepends a CODEX-OFFLOAD preamble naming the OpenAI model and
codex._comment7: effort. That agent shells out and relays the answer verbatim.
codex._comment8: The relay agent. Must exist in agents/ and be symlinked into the config dir.
codex._comment9: Only generic types offload: a specialised built-in's system prompt would be
codex._comment10: discarded by the swap, which is the whole value of using it.
codex._comment11: Tier -> OpenAI model and reasoning effort. Slugs verified against
codex._comment13: Tiers that offload AUTOMATICALLY, with no [gpt] tag. Empty means the tag is
codex._comment14: the only route in — the mechanism is live but nothing moves to OpenAI until
codex._comment15: you opt a tier in. ["opus"] reaches 18 agent-tool spawns, $105.22 in the
codex._comment16: measured window. NOT the 126 workflow opus spawns ($228.49): the workflow
codex._comment17: shim rewrites model and effort but never calls resolveCodexOffload, so no
codex._comment18: agent() call inside a script can offload today. Implementing that is the
codex._comment19: obvious next step and would roughly triple the reachable saving.
codex._comment20: haiku is deliberately excluded from autoTiers even if listed: scout spawns
codex._comment21: cost $6.77 across 13 completes, and a subprocess round-trip is slower than
codex._comment22: just running them. Offloading them would trade money you are not spending

agy._comment1: Offload to Google Antigravity through ~/.local/bin/agy, never the unrelated /usr/local/bin desktop launcher.

sandbox._comment: Linux bubblewrap is mandatory: agy is unavailable when this executable is absent.

workflow._comment1: agent() calls inside a Workflow never reach the Agent tool, and an unset
workflow._comment2: model inherits the SESSION model. Measured on one developer's machines before
workflow._comment3: install: 304 workflow agents had run on the most expensive tier for this reason.
workflow._comment4: enforce=true rewrites the script, injecting a shim that scores each prompt
workflow._comment5: at runtime and fills in model+effort where the call did not set them.
workflow._comment6: A call's own MODEL is never overridden; an effort it left unset is filled in
workflow._comment6b: from effortByTier, which is the only route to a fable workflow agent.
workflow._comment7: Set false to fall back to the old advisory behaviour (brief + deny).
workflow._comment8: Effort is settable per agent() on this path — unlike the Agent tool, whose
workflow._comment9: schema rejects the field. This is the only place effort can be tiered directly.
workflow._comment11: fable dropped high -> medium 2026-09-16: same over-thinking signature as the
workflow._comment12: tag:hard population. Raise it back if workflow fable agents start failing.
workflow._comment10: Deny is now only the fallback for scripts the rewriter cannot prove safe.
